chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: A TV commentator calls jazz noise; Buddy Collette
summary: Thompson recalls a TV commentator who knew nothing about jazz and called Buddy Collette's playing noise, and says he wants to help people understand jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: For instance recently there was a girl, a TV commentator, who was going around to the different places where they played jazz, and she had been given this

appointment from her TV sponsors, and program directors, to listen to jazz music, which was very hard to me because it seems as though they would have chosen someone who knew the music or understood it. But she admitted that she knew not the first thing about it, and evidently she didn't know anything about any kind of music because anybody who knows anything about music has to have some appreciation for jazz music.

But she could only see that jazz music was noise, because she went around to several places, and she classified it all as the same. And in one of those particular places that she went to was one of the most famous and the most equipped musical jazz groups in the world. In the person of Buddy Collette, C-o-l-l-e-t-t-e, or how many "l"s?
Yes, right, that's how it's spelled.
He's a famous saxophonist, who plays all kinds of music.

He plays in famous TV orchestra, and he reads music, he plays classical music, and he plays beautiful music. And she categorized him in some music which she had heard, which was maybe noisy, but he doesn't even play noisy music. But as far as she was concerned it was all noise.

So this is what I say, I'd like to be able to say something and explain something about jazz music in my conversation with you that might give some people some better understanding of what it's like, because jazz music is really beautiful music if it's played right.
